help.title: Format
help.optional: Examples and groups are optional: “apple || яблоко” is already a card.
help.examples: Several examples — separated by <>, the highlighted word — in [brackets].
help.forms: Three verb forms — joined by _: go_went_gone.
help.tags: Groups — with or without #, separated by spaces or commas. Nested — with /: #travel/airport.
help.comments: Empty lines and lines starting with // are skipped.

add.exampleText:
// example — feel free to delete
apple || яблоко || I eat an [apple] every day <> An [apple] a day || #food #nouns
run || бежать || I [run] in the morning || #verbs
go_went_gone || идти || I [go] home <> I [went] home <> I have [gone] home || #verbs

study.title: Study cards
study.subtitle: Concepts, definitions and theorems with Markdown and math.
study.chooseGroup: Choose or create a group to add cards.
study.emptyGroups: Create a group such as Statistics, then add subgroups for its topics.
study.emptyCards: Add a card or paste several records using bulk entry.
study.groupHelp: Up to three levels. Groups can contain cards and subgroups. Practice includes the entire subtree.
study.deleteGroupHelp: Only empty groups can be deleted. Move their cards and subgroups first.
study.deleteCardHelp: Delete this card? This cannot be undone.
study.markdownHelp: Markdown: headings, lists, tables, links, code and images. Math: $…$, $$…$$, \(…\), \[…\]. Supports KaTeX TeX, not full LaTeX; HTML is displayed as text. Invalid math is shown in red.
study.syntax: Start each record with [type: definition] (or [тип: определение]). The first --- line outside code or math blocks separates the sides. The next type header starts a new card.
study.example:
[type: theorem]
Law of large numbers
---
Under suitable conditions $\overline{X}_n \to \mathbb{E}X$.

[type: definition]
Norm
---
$$\lVert x \rVert = \sqrt{\sum_i x_i^2}$$
study.escapeHelp: Type headers and --- start at column zero. Use \--- for a literal separator on the front, and \[type: …] for a literal header. Later --- lines on the back are Markdown. Markers inside ``` and ~~~ blocks are ignored. Fix all errors before saving.
study.shortcuts: Enter / space — reveal; 1 — recalled (+1); 2 — not recalled (−1). Missed cards stay in the queue until recalled.
study.priorityHelp: Lowest scores first; ties go to the least recently reviewed cards. New cards: 0; recalled: +1; not recalled: −1. Missed cards return after three other questions, or sooner in a shorter queue.

grammar.bulkSyntax: Start each rule with [type: grammar_rule]. Add the title on the next line, then --- and the explanation.
grammar.bulkExample:
[type: grammar_rule]
Should + verb
---
Use this construction for advice or recommendations.

[formula] Subject + should + base verb
[example] You should study. || Тебе следует заниматься.
[mistake] You should to study. || You should study.

[type: grammar_rule]
Although
---
Introduces a concession.
[example] Although it was late, we stayed.

studyStats.title: Card statistics
studyStats.subtitle: Your practice activity and recall.
studyStats.emptyHelp: Rate cards during practice to see results here. Practice before this feature was added is not included.
studyStats.calendarHelp: Columns are weeks, Monday–Sunday from top to bottom. Darker means more answers. Select a day to see its totals.
studyStats.countHelp: Each rated presentation counts separately, including repeat passes. Incomplete practice counts too. This is self-assessment, not an automated knowledge check.
studyStats.knowledgeHelp: All-time answers for the current library: new — no answers; needs work — score < 0; consolidating — 0–4; confident — 5+. These are self-assessment bands, not a knowledge test.
studyStats.scoreHelp: 10 reviewed cards with the lowest all-time scores. Score = recalled answers − mistakes, including repeats. Practice selects the lowest scores across the library, including new cards.
studyStats.noRanked: No rated cards yet. Start practicing to see priorities.
